newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - COPPER, ALUMINIUM ON SHAKY GROUND.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - COPPER, ALUMINIUM ON SHAKY GROUND.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Aluminium could be due for more probes below $1,700 a tonne as the market corrects from an over-extended rally, with Tuesday's low of $1,693 the first port of call on the downside, analysts said.
Copper also remained vulnerable on Wednesday despite displaying resilience amid Tuesday's weakness across the complex.
ALUMINIUM - The market might have more work to do on the downside after Tuesday's correction lower, particularly after the Wednesday morning stock rise of 4,100 tonnes, analysts said.

"On the charts, support below $1,700 has contained the downside reaction but further probes are likely as the market has failed to close above the 10-day moving average (at $1,731). Erratic moves between support at $1,685 and resistance at $1,730 are likely," brokers Brandeis said
Relieving some pressure, the 14-day RSI had finally moved out of overbought territory and was indicated at 59 at the close of business on Tuesday.
Three months aluminium was quoted at $1,709 at 0800 GMT, compared to $1,715 at Tuesday's kerb close.
COPPER - Technical charts showed a limited upside for copper, which was trading in a $2,250-$2,300 range, analysts siad.
Some chartists said the $2,270 level -- tested but not conclusively broken on Tuesday -- remained an important gauge for copper.
"The market could break either way. If $2,270 fails to hold again, falls to trendline support at $2,240 and lower could be seen," said Harry Creates of Amalagamated Metal Trading Ltd.
At 0800 GMT three months copper was quoted at $2,267 per tonne, compared to $2,278 at the kerb close.
